title: Token economics sensitivity scenarios
summary: Working draft comparing scenario-level tradeoffs between latency percentiles and per-token unit cost across batching, KV cache hit rates, and quantization. Includes text-based charts and recommended next experiments.
body:
Background and goal:
This doc collects scenario-level comparisons for product-facing messaging and for ops to use when sizing Dedicated or private deployments. Focus is on: how P50/P95/P99 move with batching and KV cache hit rate, and how that maps to $/1M tokens under our cost model (GPU runtime + network + infra overhead).

Key assumptions (baseline):
- model: open-llama-13b-quant+opt (baseline runtime profile we tested)
- seq length: 1) short (64 tokens total) 2) medium (256 tokens) 3) long (1024 tokens)
- infrastructure cost baseline: $3.2 / GPU-hour effective (amortized across utilization)
- token pricing in calc: run-time compute cost + 10% infra overhead + network egress estimate
- batching: continuous-batching with target batch sizes and dynamic latency SLOs
- KV cache hit rate scenarios: 0%, 30%, 70% (representative of cold->warm conversational workloads)

Executive numbers snapshot (select cells, numbers rounded):
- Metric columns: scenario | P50 (ms) | P95 (ms) | P99 (ms) | tokens-per-second (eff) | $ / 1M tokens

Table: short context (64 tokens)
| scenario                     | P50  | P95  | P99  | tps  | $/1M |
|------------------------------|------|------|------|------|------|
| baseline (no cache, batch 1) | 42ms | 110ms| 220ms| 18   | $42  |
| small-batch (batch 8)        | 52ms | 120ms| 250ms| 64   | $14  |
| aggressive-batch (batch 32)  | 120ms| 320ms| 720ms| 180  | $6.5 |
| kv-cache 30% + batch 8       | 38ms | 95ms | 200ms| 85   | $11  |
| kv-cache 70% + batch 8       | 28ms | 65ms | 120ms| 120  | $6.5 |
| int8-quantized (batch 8)     | 36ms | 90ms | 190ms| 95   | $5.8 |

Interpretation (short context):
- Batch size drives tokens/sec strongly but shifts tail latency; P95/P99 grow nonlinearly with large batches when request variance is high.
- KV cache is multiplier-friendly: 70% hit rate reduces effective work by ~4x vs cold, shifting both latency and cost dramatically.
- Quantization yields a steady improvement in cost but doesn't change the variance profile.

Table: medium context (256 tokens)
| scenario                     | P50  | P95  | P99  | tps  | $/1M |
|------------------------------|------|------|------|------|------|
| baseline (no cache, batch 1) | 130ms| 360ms| 820ms| 8    | $86  |
| small-batch (batch 8)        | 200ms| 490ms| 1200ms| 40  | $22  |
| aggressive-batch (batch 24)  | 420ms| 980ms| 2400ms| 120| $8.5 |
| kv-cache 30% + batch 8       | 110ms| 290ms| 650ms| 55   | $22  |
| kv-cache 70% + batch 8       | 85ms | 210ms| 420ms| 88   | $11  |
| int8-quantized (batch 8)     | 95ms | 240ms| 520ms| 95   | $9.8 |

Interpretation (medium context):
- For longer contexts, absolute latency increases and batching benefits are stronger for cost but start to create multi-second tails at high batches.
- KV cache remains the single biggest lever for both latency and cost for conversational workloads.

Table: long context (1024 tokens)
| scenario                     | P50   | P95   | P99   | tps   | $/1M |
|------------------------------|-------|-------|-------|-------|------|
| baseline (no cache, batch 1) | 510ms | 1380ms| 3200ms| 1.9   | $420 |
| small-batch (batch 4)        | 680ms | 1600ms| 3800ms| 7.5   | $110 |
| aggressive-batch (batch 12)  | 1200ms| 3200ms| 7400ms| 24    | $36  |
| kv-cache 30% + batch 4       | 420ms | 1150ms| 2900ms| 12.5  | $96  |
| kv-cache 70% + batch 4       | 310ms | 780ms | 1600ms| 18.2  | $52  |
| int8-quantized (batch 4)     | 290ms | 700ms | 1500ms| 20    | $34  |

Interpretation (long context):
- Long contexts magnify absolute latency and cost; here the only scalable path to keep latencies sub-second is cache hits and smaller batches. Aggressive batching reduces $/token but produces long tails that may violate SLOs.

Simple ASCII latency curve (P50->P99) for medium context, baseline -> kv70 -> int8 (approx, scaled):
P50: baseline [=====     ] 130ms -> kv70 [==       ] 85ms -> int8 [==       ] 95ms
P95: baseline [==========] 360ms -> kv70 [=====    ] 210ms -> int8 [======   ] 240ms
P99: baseline [==============] 820ms -> kv70 [========= ] 420ms -> int8 [========  ] 520ms
(visual only — rough comparison of relative length)

Cost sensitivity heatmap (qualitative):
- Red: high $/1M (> $100), Orange: mid ($30-$100), Green: low (< $30)
- Short context: baseline=Orange, batch32=Green, kv70/int8=Green
- Medium context: baseline=Red, batch24=Orange, kv70/int8=Green-Orange
- Long context: baseline=Red, batch12=Orange, kv70/int8=Orange

Operational notes and recommended messaging for sales & docs:
- Messaging: 'Cache-aware serving provides up to 4x effective token throughput for conversational apps' (note: support with example percentages above).
- For customers with latency-sensitive SLAs (P95 < 500ms), recommend: small batches (<=8), enable KV cache, quantize if model fidelity acceptable.
- For cost-sensitive but latency-tolerant workloads (batch-processed embeddings or backend inference), recommend aggressive batching + int8 quantization.

Open questions / next experiments (prioritized):
1) Measure live tail behavior under mixed-size arrivals with bursty diurnal patterns (ticket: JIRA SRV-1427) — hypothesize P99 will degrade faster than simulated steady-state.
2) Repeat same scenario curves for 7B and 70B family models to confirm scaling multipliers (cost and latency).
3) Add network egress variance (cross-region fallback) to the model; estimate 15-40ms added P50 for cross-region.
4) Run A/B with alternate continuous-batching heuristics and SLO-aware batch-cut logic (experiment: github PR 4819).

Appendix: brief methodology notes
- Measurements were taken on a dev cluster that mirrors Dedicated node spec (A100-like) using synthetic arrival traces (Poisson + burst episodes) and a replay trace from a production customer (anonymized).
- Cost calc uses measured GPU utilization * hourly cost + 10% infra overhead + tokenization/network estimate.
- 'tokens-per-second' is measured effective token throughput including both input and output tokens.

Quick TODOs for this doc (me/ops):

Notes to reviewers: draft — numbers are approximate and intended to calibrate tradeoffs. Please comment inline or add tickets for deeper investigation.

-- Sofia
